[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Actapio, Inc. is a wholly owned US subsidiary of LY Corporation, the Japanese technology company formerly known as Z Holdings and, before that, Yahoo Japan Corporation. Actapio operates data center capacity in Washington State, with third-party facility tracking placing its campus in the Wenatchee and Douglas County area at approximately 16 megawatts of critical IT load on a 20 acre site, a figure this registry treats as a lead pending direct confirmation rather than a verified fact from Actapio or LY Corporation directly. The companys own site describes its Washington location as chosen for access to low cost, clean hydroelectric power, which reduces operating costs relative to running equivalent infrastructure in Japan. Actapios stated services include cloud computing, computer system and server rentals, and application hosting, built on open source infrastructure, and it has been covered in AI and open compute industry press for GPU-based automation work supporting its parent companys AI models. Beyond hosting, Actapio also runs a secondary consulting business helping American startups expand into the Japanese market, drawing on LY Corporations established presence there. As a hyperscale parents dedicated US infrastructure subsidiary rather than a third-party colocation provider, Actapios role in this registry is closest to the other corporate-captive operators already profiled, such as the hyperscalers, though at a much smaller single-site scale. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project. This session made a further attempt to resolve a building specific street address. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned a single, 0.9 confidence candidate, 207 N United Sakura Dr, East Wenatchee, WA 98802, a street name notable for its own Japanese themed name given this operators Japanese parent company, though this is a coincidental naming observation rather than confirming evidence. A data center industry tracker already on file as a source for this operator separately gives coordinates for its Wenatchee area facility about seven kilometers from this rows own stored coordinates, close enough to plausibly describe the same single-site operator but not precise enough to confirm this exact address, and states 20 acres and 16 MW without publishing a street address. Given no second, independent source corroborates the geocoded street address, it is not applied, consistent with this projects standard that a geocoding services own confidence score is not itself external corroboration.
